title: Runtime vocabulary/domain learning and Goblin/Millwood knowledge-barrier fixtures

sections.what: Wire organic runtime acquisition of foreign vocabulary and domain knowledge as character memories (from conversational context, gestures, and reading educational materials/phrasebooks/manuals - not via CraftingSystem.teach) and author verified Goblin/Millwood knowledge-barrier fixtures.
sections.why: Static competence sheets go stale quickly unless characters can learn words and craft/trade facts in play, and AGENTS.md rule 8 requires concrete authored fixtures alongside mechanism tests. Extending the existing CraftingSystem.teach command, examine/read grants, and _teach_* hooks avoids inventing new one-off subsystems while proving both target settings end-to-end.
sections.how: 1. Keep CraftingSystem.teach scoped to recipes/skills; do NOT add teach lang:<id>:<word> commands.\n2. Treat language and domain knowledge as memory (per task-734): when a character reads educational materials (phrasebooks, manuals, textbooks) via examine/read, or encounters foreign words in clear conversational/gestural context, record semantic/episodic memory entries that unlock understood words/concepts organically.\n3. Author concrete reference fixtures across Millwood (Sammy, Kayla, Zoe) and Goblin/bilingual exchange characters with asymmetrical domain competence, explicit blind spots, and partial vocabulary verified end-to-end by tests.
sections.verify:
1. Run pytest covering teach lang:<id>:<word>, teach domain:<id>, examine phrasebook/manual learning, and full Goblin/exchange-student speech masking plus Millwood Sammy/Kayla/Zoe domain asymmetry fixtures.
2. Verify python tools/lint_library.py passes after updating character fixtures.

acceptance.text: Foreign vocabulary and domain understanding are acquired through memory and lived context (conversational context, object pointing, or reading educational materials/phrasebooks/manuals), NOT via CraftingSystem.teach (which remains dedicated to recipes/skills)
Reading/examining educational materials or experiencing contextual word usage creates semantic/episodic memories that update the character's understood vocabulary and persist across save/load

Millwood character fixtures (Sammy, Kayla, Zoe) and Goblin/bilingual exchange fixtures carry concrete domain competence, explicit ignorant blind spots, and partial known vocabulary verified end-to-end by tests

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Human Turn / Agent Turn Composer (teach and read/examine actions), Character Inspector -> Mind -> Persona (Languages & Domains updates at runtime), and Prompt Lens.

Current availability: CraftingSystem.teach in engine/crafting.py (lines 368-406) and routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1118-1127) only accept recipes and skill:<name>, and shipped characters in data/library/characters/ have 0 language lexicons or domain expertise/ignorance profiles.

Manual verification steps:
1. Load Sammy, Kayla, Zoe, or a Goblin/exchange-student pair in a test scenario and inspect Persona Languages/Domains plus Prompt Lens before interaction.
   - expected: Sammy shows skateboarding competence and computing ignorance; Kayla shows legal/language competence and DIY/physics ignorance; Zoe shows silicone_molding/DIY competence and sports ignorance; partial foreign speakers show initial known_words only.
2. Execute 'teach lang:english:silicone to Kenji' (or have Zoe demonstrate/teach DIY curing to Kayla) when co-located.
   - expected: Target character's live known_words or domain/semantic memory updates and persists across save/load, and subsequent WITNESSED speech or examine output reflects the newly learned term.
